newsitem.title: FRANCE: French birth rate rises for second successive year.
newsitem.headline: French birth rate rises for second successive year.

text.p: France's birth rate rose in 1996 for the second successive year, taking the population to 58.5 million, the French Statistics Institute (INSEE ) said on Tuesday.

The birth rate hit a trough in 1994 but began rising again in 1995 as the figures kept falling in all other European Union countries except Greece and Ireland, INSEE said. It gave no EU statistics for last year.
A total of 734,000 children were born in France last year, 6,000 more than in 1995. INSEE said the extra day in leap year 1996 accounted for 2,000 births.
INSEE said life expectancy had reached 74 years for men and 82 for women. It was rising by about three months every year, with men slowly closing the gap.
The number of foreigners in the country rose by 40,000, the same increase as last year but half the rate of the early 1990s. France passed tough legislation in 1993 to curb immigration.
